title: Rav Chanan bar Moladah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rav Chanan bar Moladah speaks in Rav Huna’s name in two rulings in [Sanhedrin 70a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.70a.6-7). [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Sanhedrin.70a.7.1) explains that Moladah is his father’s name. Hyman reports that the old printings have Rabbi Yochanan bar Molada. He traces the error to the Soncino printing, which had Rav Yachnan, and says that the yod dropped from the word Rav, producing “Yochanan.” He cites Dikdukei Soferim.

notes.text: The [Dikdukei Soferim page](https://books.google.com/books?id=cIKZ30PgAHMC&pg=RA2-PP1) records the competing names in its apparatus on Sanhedrin 70a. Hyman’s explanation of the dropped letter remains a separate report.
The two statements cited in the linked Bavli are both introduced as transmissions from Rav Huna. In the consulted Rashi, Moladah is explained as Chanan’s father’s name.

Dikdukei Soferim on Sanhedrin 70a (p. ק, note ר) reports Rabbi Chanan bar Molada for both occurrences in two manuscripts. It reports Rav Yochanan in the first occurrence in the old printings other than Constantinople. It traces that form to Soncino’s Rav Yachnan and reads Rabbi Chanan, as in the nearby Soncino occurrence. Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 471) says that the yod dropped from Rav. The apparatus records the forms and its proposed reading; the Soncino page itself has not been independently collated. The consulted Sanhedrin 70a has Chanan reporting in Rav Huna’s name in both passages.
